question: Can artifacts/kaggle/p0strict_cache (199 post-wrapper OOF graphs) carry arm B?
verdict: NO. It is a POST-wrapper surface and arm B edits a PRE-wrapper stage.

1_no_edge_prob.why_it_matters: the P0 relink cost is motion + 0.05*raw - 1.0*prob (BIOHUB_MOTION_RELINK_LEARNED_BONUS=1.0, vs 0.75 on E0c). With no probabilities the learned term is identically zero for BOTH arms, so any delta measured there belongs to a different cost function.

2_wrong_node_population.why_it_matters: motion_relink_edges runs on the raw detector node set. 83,260 nodes (4.25%) are pruned/short-track-filtered away before the cache exists, and 26,122 synthetic gap-close nodes are added after the relink has already run.

3_coordinates_have_moved.why_it_matters: the gate is a distance in um computed from these coordinates. 92.0% of them have been linefit-smoothed and then written as max(0,int(round(v))); the median move is 0.575 um against a 6.0 um radius.

4_edges_are_already_relink_output.note: filter_output_graph line: edges = motion_edges. The cache edge list IS the relink result, so re-gating it is a SECOND relink of an already-relinked graph.

5_empirical_parity.test: re-run the DEPLOYED motion_relink_edges (comp=0, the identity operation) on the cached node set and compare per-crop counters with the published anchors
5_empirical_parity.reading: the identity operation already breaks per-crop parity on 3 of 3 6bba crops - the family carrying 85.06% of edge mass. WS-F non-negotiable 1 aborts here.

what_WS_B_actually_did: WS-B re-ran ONLY OUTPUT_PRUNE_ISOLATED + filter_short_track_components on this cache and relied on refilter_identity being True (the cache is a fixed point of that node filter). It never re-ran motion relink, gap close, gap2, safe divisions or linefit - those stages have no inputs on a post-wrapper surface. Its result is sound for suppress-all, which is a pure topology edit, and gives no licence for a pre-wrapper gate change.
